security_audit.summary: Most alerts are false positives from Markdown, comments, CSS, loopback addresses, and local screenshot workflows. Confirmed risks include unchecked process termination, path-based JavaScript injection, inherited credentials, and permission bypass without isolation. Additional findings cover unsafe cleanup and unescaped viewer content; no evidence of covert upload or audit-directed prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Untrusted executors bypass host permission checks.
remediation.suggestion: Default to restricted permissions. Run untrusted skill evaluation in an isolated container or virtual machine with explicit filesystem and network limits.

remediation.issue: Executor and snapshot subprocesses inherit potentially sensitive environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Build an environment allowlist containing only required tool paths and evaluation settings. Exclude unrelated tokens and credentials.

remediation.issue: Snapshot scripts interpolate project paths into JavaScript source.
remediation.suggestion: Pass project paths through process.argv and parse app.json as data. Do not concatenate paths into node -e source.

remediation.issue: Port cleanup can kill unrelated services.
remediation.suggestion: Track processes started by the run and terminate only those process groups. Reject occupied ports instead of forcibly clearing them.

remediation.issue: Fixture cleanup uses substring checks and shared DerivedData patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Require an ownership marker and canonical workspace containment. Reject symlink escapes and delete only the run-specific DerivedData directory.

remediation.issue: Viewer rendering trusts raw prompts and generated grading text.
remediation.suggestion: Escape all text and attribute values. Add a restrictive Content Security Policy and render untrusted results without executable markup.

remediation.issue: Emulator recovery terminates shared Android resources.
remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated emulator serial and tracked process identifier. Require explicit consent before resetting the shared adb server.

content.user_title: Evaluate Expo Skills with Code and Screenshot Tests
content.value_statement: Expo skill changes can affect triggering, generated code, and rendered screens. This skill guides paired evaluations with code checks, runtime screenshots, and evidence-based grading.
actual_capabilities: Guide trigger recall tests through Claude CLI streams using the local Expo plugin.
Create cached Expo fixtures for paired runs with and without the selected skill.
Run TypeScript checks, changed-file linting, and platform bundle exports.
Capture initial-route screenshots on iOS, Android, and optional web targets.
Grade screenshots against expectations and optional reference images using a documented design rubric.
Generate a self-contained HTML viewer with paired results, iteration tabs, and trigger metrics.
limitations: Executors require Claude CLI, Python, and Bun. iOS screenshots require macOS and Xcode; Android requires an SDK and emulator.
Snapshot scripts capture only the initial route and cannot tap controls or navigate through an app.
Trigger evaluation measures recall only. It does not measure false-positive triggering.
Native builds require substantial time and disk space. Unrestricted subprocesses need external isolation to protect the host.

use_cases.title: Compare a skill revision
use_cases.description: Compare generated apps with and without an edited Expo skill using consistent prompts, fixtures, and code checks.

use_cases.title: Review reference-image fidelity
use_cases.description: Evaluate how closely a generated Expo screen matches a supplied image across selected platforms.

use_cases.title: Check generated code without devices
use_cases.description: Run type checks, changed-file linting, and bundle exports before scheduling slower simulator or emulator evaluations.

prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [skill] with one built-in prompt using code checks only. Use the latest Expo SDK and restricted permissions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with a small evaluation that needs no device.

prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [skill] against a baseline for a settings screen. Capture the root route on iOS and Android with Expo Go. Keep results local.
prompt_templates.scenario: Check visible behavior on both native platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Compare a reference image
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [skill] against [reference image path] on iOS. Compare reference fidelity and design quality with the baseline. Keep the viewer local.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review visual quality using a specific target screen.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Run a controlled benchmark
prompt_templates.prompt: Benchmark [skill] across [prompts] on SDK [version]. Measure trigger recall, code checks, and selected runtime platforms. Use isolated restricted executors. Capture timing and tokens.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare a skill revision using controlled settings and recorded metrics.

output_examples.input: Check an Expo routing skill with code checks only.
output: Illustrative result: the skill-assisted app passes type checking and linting.
The baseline fails bundle export because an import cannot be resolved.
The local viewer shows paired build status and grading evidence.

output_examples.input: Compare a generated settings screen against a reference image on iOS.
output: Illustrative result: the generated screen matches the reference grouping and toggle placement.
Reference fidelity loses points for different spacing and accent colors.
The viewer displays the target image, generated screenshots, and design rubric scores.

output_examples.input: Measure whether an Expo skill triggers on representative prompts.
output: Illustrative result: the target skill triggers on four of five should-trigger prompts.
Trigger recall is 80 percent; the missed prompt is listed for review.
False-positive triggering is not measured by this run.

best_practices: Use an isolated machine or virtual environment, restricted permissions, and an environment without unrelated credentials.
Keep prompts, SDK versions, and platforms consistent between paired runs. Render the tested feature at the initial route.
Inspect screenshots and logs before accepting scores. Review viewer content and obtain explicit approval before publishing results.
anti_patterns: Treating a temporary working directory as a security sandbox for permission-skipping executors.
Placing the tested screen behind navigation that snapshot scripts cannot perform.
Creating cached fixtures concurrently or running native snapshots in parallel on shared devices.

faq.question: What does this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It guides trigger recall, generated code checks, runtime screenshots, and optional reference-image grading for Expo skills.

faq.question: Does evaluation require a simulator?
faq.answer: No. Code checks and trigger tests can run without a simulator. Runtime screenshots require the selected native device tooling or web browser.

faq.question: Can it evaluate custom native code?
faq.answer: Development builds can evaluate custom native code with the required toolchain. Expo Go supports only its bundled native capabilities.

faq.question: Can snapshots test interactions?
faq.answer: No. Snapshot scripts capture the initial route. They do not tap, scroll, or navigate.

faq.question: Are screenshots published automatically?
faq.answer: Artifact publishing requires explicit opt-in. The default viewer is local, but executors and dependency installation may still use network services.

faq.question: Can Codex run the whole workflow alone?
faq.answer: The documented executor and trigger phases invoke Claude CLI. Codex does not replace that dependency in the supplied workflow.
